<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**13** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895dd437f4b50402dddf6b147190c2b5d24e85ef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `21aa703abe43162ef10dc70061733edcc8dc303b` — the merge of head `b1c6a5bc1211f02b4f156b954792c44f43d7cf16` into base `895dd437f4b50402dddf6b147190c2b5d24e85ef`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 21aa703abe43162ef10dc70061733edcc8dc303b && git checkout 21aa703abe43162ef10dc70061733edcc8dc303b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 895dd437f4b50402dddf6b147190c2b5d24e85ef b1c6a5bc1211f02b4f156b954792c44f43d7cf16 && git checkout -B drift-repro 895dd437f4b50402dddf6b147190c2b5d24e85ef && git merge --no-ff b1c6a5bc1211f02b4f156b954792c44f43d7cf16

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895dd437f4b50402dddf6b147190c2b5d24e85ef
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：安装或升级一个包时，如果新版本新增了"自动计算并保存"的字段（或把公式字段改成这种字段），已有的数据会在安装时一次性算好填上，所有组织都会处理，不改动记录的"最后修改时间"；以前这些旧数据会一直是空的。
- 为什么做：按你之前的裁决，保存元数据时会补算，安装时也应该补算；托管环境上原来根本没有办法补。
- 出错会怎样：补算失败不会让安装失败，安装结果里会列出哪些字段没补完，以及补算的命令。
- 要你做什么：无。区域自行落地。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT** · head `b1c6a5bc1211f02b4f156b954792c44f43d7cf16` · Fixes #35390 (#32527 ruling 6816429574 letter A at the install door) · 2026-11-19T13:35Z

Readings: K=3; `check-governed-merges --pr 35514` not governed; `merge-tree` against main clean; CI 41 success / 17 skipped / 1 in progress / 0 failed. Land it on full green.

**Code (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, +206).**
- Step 2g captures `captureStoredExpressions(object)` for every object the incoming body contributes to (`contributionsOf`: own objects and extension targets, every unit of a composed artifact). It runs BEFORE the register and reads definitions only. An engine without the member yields `[]`.
- Step 4d calls `fillChanged()` per capture. It runs after the schema sync, the datasources and the handler bind, and before the seed, so a fresh table answers clean and seeded rows compute through their own writes. The walk is the engine's, the one `os migrate stored-expressions --changed --apply` runs, under `preserveAudit` and over every organization.
- A failed schema sync is recorded and nothing is filled; each changed field is reported unfilled, with "resolve the sync first".
- A throwing fill is logged and reported per field. Neither case fails the install or stops the other objects.
- `stored-expression-filled` (info) or `stored-expression-fill-incomplete` (warning) is emitted per field, the second naming what is left and the exact command. `os migrate stored-expressions` has `--object`, `--field`, `--changed` and `--apply`, checked against `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-expressions.ts:80-96`.
- A register refusal returns before 4d, so it fills nothing.

**Pins.** `…install-local-stored-expression-fill.test.ts`, 7 cases:
- v1 formula → v2 stored fills every row of both organizations once, keeps `updated_at`, and reports per field;
- an added stored field is filled, while the unchanged one beside it is not re-walked;
- a composed-artifact unit is filled;
- a re-install over kept rows is filled;
- CONTROLs: no stored change gives no row and no `advisories`; a refused upgrade gives 422 and no row; a fresh empty table gives no `advisories`.

The report shows red-first (7010586784).

**The judgment asked: `Clause-②: no` is confirmed, and no L2 is owed.** `advisories` is an optional key on this door's own JSON answer. It is left out when empty, so every existing answer keeps its key set. Its element type (`InstallStoredExpressionAdvisory`) is module-private, not exported, and no `packages/spec` schema declares the door's answer. It is the same posture as this door's `renamesCarried`, which shipped under `Clause-②: no` (cloud-connection CHANGELOG). The widening rule I apply to a published export gaining a member does not reach an undeclared, unexported answer key. `Metadata-protocol: none`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection` patch.

**Changeset and docs: sentences checked against the diff.**
- The changeset's capture scope, fill timing, `updated_at`, every organization, the two rule ids, "omitted when there is nothing to report", the three no-write cases and "never fails the install" all match the code and the pins.
- `publish-and-preview.mdx`: the rename bullet is the existing behaviour (`--confirm-upgrade` is at `cli.mdx:3613`), and the fill bullet matches the changeset.
- Nit (non-blocking): "a boot or a restart never fills … and the boot log names the field" is half right. The boot sample (`stored-expression-backfill.ts:954`) names fields holding NULL, not rows holding an old expression's value. Narrow that sentence to the NULL case when convenient.

**Routing.** Not governed, no contract face: pkg-1 lands it. Follow-ups #35517 and #35518 (p3) are noted. A new push needs a fresh L1 only if it changes more than a main merge.
